Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for acute left-sided headache that woke patient at ~5:30 AM; more severe than prior headaches, with mild photophobia and initial dizziness (resolved). No fever or neck stiffness; paracetamol provided little relief.
- Clinical impression: tension-type headache vs migraine. Plan: trial ibuprofen, optional continuation of paracetamol, stress reduction (consider 1-week self-certified leave), counseling self-referral, optimize sleep and hydration. Follow-up in 1 week; safety-netting provided.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute left-sided headache
  - Onset: woke patient around 5:30 AM (earlier than usual 7 AM wake time).
  - Course: still present at time of consult; more severe than prior headaches.
  - Character/location: left-sided; prior headaches typically across the front (“cluster at the front”), less severe.
  - Associated symptoms: mild photophobia; initial dizziness on waking (subsided); no nausea; no fever; no neck stiffness.
  - Positional: initially more sore when lying down, then improves; overall better when lying down.
  - Medications tried: paracetamol taken this morning with minimal relief.
  - Family history: no known migraines.
  - Differential: tension-type headache vs migraine (discussed by clinician).
  - Management advice:
    - Start ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented); may continue paracetamol if desired.
    - Sleep 7–8 hours nightly; hydrate 1.5–2 L/day (excluding coffee/tea).
    - Safety net: provided danger symptom information; low threshold to seek reassessment if worsening or new symptoms.
    - Follow-up in 1 week; consider blood tests if not improving.

Issue 2:
- Work-related stress with history of anxiety
  - History: anxiety x ~2 years; currently on sertraline; intermittent work-related anxiety; no suicidal ideation.
  - Context: increased work stress for a couple of months; late nights and backlog of work.
  - Management advice:
    - Consider 1 week off work (self-certify) to reduce stress burden.
    - Counseling: clinician to provide link for local self-referral counseling service.
    - Reinforce sleep hygiene and hydration as above.
    - Follow-up in 1 week alongside headache review.

Issue 3:
- Prior headache history (less severe, typically frontal)
  - No prior formal migraine diagnosis reported.
  - No family history of migraine.

Medications:
- Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Paracetamol taken today for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Ibuprofen advised to start for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Note: Aspirin mentioned as guideline-supported option but not specifically advised to start.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Anxiety disorder (~2 years).
- Recurrent headaches (previously less severe; typically frontal).

Social History:
- Lives with partner.
- Non-smoker.
- Exercises: running ~3 times/week.
- Diet: “OK,” not particularly healthy but not unhealthy (per patient).
- Work: increased stress and late nights for ~2 months.
- Pets: cat.

Preventative History:
- Not documented: cervical screening test, mammogram, prostate blood test, fecal occult blood test, bone mineral density, vaccinations.
- Not documented: recent optometry review or skin check.

Physical Examination:
- No in-person examination performed (telehealth).
- Vitals not recorded.

Plan:
- Start ibuprofen for suspected migraine-type headache; may continue paracetamol as needed (doses not documented).
- Stress reduction: consider 1-week self-certified leave from work.
- Counseling: clinician to provide local self-referral counseling link; patient encouraged to engage.
- Supportive care: sleep 7–8 hours nightly; hydrate 1.5–2 L/day (excluding coffee/tea).
- Follow-up: schedule review in 1 week. If not improving, consider blood tests and reassessment.
- Safety net: review provided danger signs for headaches; return sooner if worsening, new neurologic symptoms, or any concerns.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: medication doses/routes/frequencies; full neurologic review; neurologic exam; vitals (including blood pressure); comprehensive medication reconciliation (OTCs, supplements); alcohol intake not discussed.
- Internal conflicts: patient’s name referenced variably (“Atan,” “Ayrton Warren,” and addressed as “Anthony”)—conflict noted; positional effect on headache initially worse when lying down then better—clarified by patient as ultimately better when lying down.
- Transcript quality: generally clear; some brief incomplete utterances, but clinical content understandable.
